html:
The Battle of the Thames was fought on 5 October 1813 beside the Thames River near Moraviantown, in today's Ontario, Canada. A United States army under William Henry Harrison beat a British force and its Native allies. The Shawnee leader Tecumseh was killed.

It was part of the War of 1812. The British at Detroit, under General Henry Procter, were supplied across Lake Erie. When an American squadron captured the British ships on the lake in September 1813, Procter had to retreat east into Upper Canada. Tecumseh, whose warriors had fought beside the British to defend their own lands, pressed him to stand and fight. Procter had about 800 soldiers and Tecumseh about 500 warriors. Harrison followed with about 3,500 men, many of them mounted riflemen from Kentucky. Their charge broke the thin British line in minutes, and most of the soldiers surrendered. The warriors fought on in a swamp until Tecumseh fell.

Tecumseh's alliance died with him, and most of the nations made peace. Native power in the lands south of the Great Lakes was broken, and the region was opened to American settlers. Harrison, already known for Tippecanoe, later became president.
